original_text: Transair 810 primary facts (NTSB DCA21FA174 docket, data.ntsb.gov, read 25 Oct 2026): water impact 11:45:17 UTC (CVR 01:45:17 HST; ADS-B ends 11:45:17.902; FDR ends 01:45:16.94 HST, no impact spike); position 21.27616 N 158.02565 W (APG study Table 4 'Estimated water impact', ADS-B); groundspeed 114.6 kt, CAS 123 kt, pitch +12.3 deg, bank -14.9 deg, ADS-B climb rate -764 fpm; EGPWS radio altitude 64.5/55/42.5/26.5 ft at 1-s steps before contact; takeoff weight 93,557 lb; wreck 104-111 m depth, fuselage broke at BS 540 (two pieces), tail floated then sank. Kadri S1 position 21 18'41"N 157 54'16"W is near HNL airport, ~13 km from the NTSB point. original_text: Transair 810 R3 result (25 Oct 2026, note v268bb7db, pre-registration v986504a4). Predicted window, ditching site: no significant detection with limited power (M1b p 0.079 at H11N, 0.095 at H11S). Kadri Fig. 5b box: a real signal, but two pulses arrive from 152.6 deg at H11S and reach H11N 72-73 s later; the ditching would come from 79-81 deg with H11N first by 30 s. Source unidentified, possibly a Tonga-Kermadec T-phase. Measured L50 is 0.065 / 0.048 Pa (1-s RMS). Upper limit eta_rad <= 3.2e-4 (z 10 m) to 0.12 (0.5 m) at H11S, 0.14x the F-35A ridge at H11S and 0.31x at H11N, using KE 73.6 MJ (NTSB) and a source 3 km seaward because KRAKEN has no modes at <= 40 Hz on the Oahu shelf. DB rows CV26-CV35, E18 (group G9) pass the validator. Open questions: an upper-limit role in the vocabulary; total vs vertical KE as the R3 denominator.

original_text: Raw F-35A H11 re-derivation (track 1, 25 Oct 2026; note v 82598f24, EXPLORATORY, pre-registered v 493a290e). The raw exposures are 0.22-0.29 dB above the digitised Metz values. The f^-2 KRAKEN+RAM ridge is 0.229/0.0572/0.00925/0.00240/6.84e-4/3.64e-4/1.86e-4 at 1/2/5/10/20/30/50 m, about 1.06x the digitised values. The 20 Hz gap is present at all 6 elements, and it is not the instrument, the noise or the TL. Raw 2-4 Hz data give a source corner near 5 Hz. With that corner, eta is 0.6-1.0x the f^-2 value. The f^-4 family without a corner overstates eta by 37-61x and exceeds 1 at z <= 2 m. New per-triad pyram delta: H11N RAM correction is 1-3 dB smaller than H11S; using each triad's own delta cuts the N/S eta ratio from 2.16 to 1.26 (10 m eta 1.81e-3). The FDSN-coordinate back-azimuth is 3-4 deg clockwise of Metz and geodesic (unresolved). Raw-peak Arons D2 is 5.4e-4 (4-64 Hz), against Brown's 2.08e-4.

original_text: M1b real-arrival test (25 Oct 2026): the San Juan event gives p = 0.0026 (floor, n = 379) at all five usable H10 elements; the charge gives p = 0.0027-0.0082 (n = 363). Same-day background windows reach 0.93-0.98, so the amplitude-blind statistic barely separates a 16-24 dB SNR arrival (gap G11-1 confirmed). San Juan event explosion-equivalent through the chain is 9-918 kg for 200-900 m depth; Heyburn's 428 kg is reached only at ~800-900 m.

original_text: Raw-IMS level check (25 Oct 2026, note v801ac901): the stage-1b San Juan charge level FAIL (-14.4 dB) was mostly a unit conversion. Nielsen Fig 5c PSD is matched by a raw 60 s Welch PSD (-1.7 to +0.1 dB), so PSD->energy needs T ~50 s (39-71 s), not 10 s (about 7 dB). On raw data the charge residual is -2.8 to -8.2 dB at H10N and -0.9 to +5.7 dB at H10S, the spread set by the G&S source variant. Residual slope over 17 explosion-station pairs (charge, 8 FSST shots) is -3.7 to +2.9 dB/oct, so the airgun +7/+10 dB/oct slope failure is not reproduced on explosions. Proposed sigma_model is level ~5 dB plus a source term ~4 dB plus a ridge-path term >=6 dB, and slope ~1.5 dB/oct (provisional).

original_text: IMS H10S1 reads about 30 dB below H10S2/S3 in every event 2016-2021 (Nielsen 2021: electronic noise). Exclude it. H10S-H10N station difference: 2016 FSST agrees with the model within ~2 dB; 2021 FSST is 3-8 dB low at H10S, and H10S2 background is ~7 dB quieter in 2021 than in 2016-17. StationXML has one response epoch since 2004, so an H10S gain or hardware change is possible (unresolved). The South American sources show a model miss of +6.5 dB (H10S louder), attributed to unmodelled Rio Grande Rise blockage on the H10N path.

original_text: FSST shot times and positions come from USGS ComCat 'experimental explosion' rows (2016: 06-10, 06-23, 07-16, 09-04, 09-21; 2021: 06-18, 07-16, 08-08; horizontal error 3-7 km). The charge depth for 2016/2021 is not in any primary source; 61 m (200 ft) is from the 2008 FSST notice 73 FR 43129. The FSST level moves ~11 dB over 30-100 m depth. At 61 m the inverted 5-40 Hz radiated energy exceeds the explosive energy at 4/15 pairs (KRAKEN) and 3/4 (RAM), so the chain is too lossy on the Blake Plateau paths or the charges were deeper.
